title: Student status; rural living; transportation
description: Hollis Edgerton confirms she is a second-year student at Lewis and Clark College. She explains that she prefers living on the farm for the open space and solitude, and now has her own car to travel 30 miles to school from Genesee, which gives her independence.

title: Summer jobs; driving truck; gender differences
description: Hollis describes her work history, including a job at the Rose Hours Bakery in Moscow and helping with farm chores. She drives trucks on the farm because she cannot lift hay bales as quickly as her brothers, and reflects on the mixed feelings of being a girl versus a boy.

title: Academic life; recreation; career uncertainty
description: Hollis discusses her general education coursework, studying habits, and social activities like drinking beer and watching basketball. She is uncertain about her career goals but knows she wants to marry someday without a clear plan for employment.

title: Women's athletics; career preparation; ideal job
description: Hollis notes the lack of girls' basketball programs at her high school and college, though she would have played if given the chance. She discusses preparing for work by taking achievement tests and considers a vocational education path, though she had previously wanted to be an elementary teacher.

title: Dormitory life; weekend activities; physical education
description: Hollis describes living in the girls' residence hall, where about 56 women live. She often goes home on weekends for better food, discusses the dorm food quality, and mentions taking physical education requirements.

title: Television habits; housing; marriage criteria
description: Hollis talks about watching soap operas and comedies in the dorm. She describes the housing situation, noting many local girls live in apartments or at home. She outlines her ideal husband as being taller than her, kind like her father, and able to support the family.

title: Family roles; decision making; women's movement
description: Hollis envisions raising children on a farm like her mother, ideally not working after marriage unless necessary. She believes wives should have equal say in family decisions. She shows little interest in the women's liberation movement, viewing it as irrelevant to her life.

title: Community attitudes; university choice
description: Hollis discusses how Genesee residents are skeptical of university interference and prefer local control over schools. She chose Lewis and Clark over the University of Idaho because it is smaller, less overwhelming, more affordable, and friendlier.
